title: An Integrated Preprocessing and Drift Detection Approach With Adaptive Windowing for Fraud Detection in Payment Systems
authors: Al Lawati, H.M.R.; Zainal, A.; Al-Rimy, B.A.S.; Al-Azawi, M.; Kassim, M.N.; Almalki, S.A.; Alghamdi, T.A.
tldr: A CNN-based fraud detection framework combines Mutual Information feature selection, ADASYN resampling, and hierarchical EDDM-ADWIN drift detection to achieve up to 99.99% accuracy across real and synthetic payment datasets.
problem_and_motivation: Static machine learning and rule-based fraud detection methods cannot capture the evolving nature of fraudulent behaviors, leading to lower accuracy and higher false positive rates.
approach: Mutual Information and SelectKBest perform supervised feature selection to identify the most relevant transaction features and reduce dimensionality.
ADASYN generates synthetic minority-class instances to address class imbalance, focusing on difficult-to-learn fraud regions.
A Convolutional Neural Network serves as the core classifier, learning complex patterns from preprocessed and balanced transaction data.
EDDM monitors error distances between prediction batches to detect gradual drift in fraud patterns over time.
ADWIN dynamically adjusts sliding window sizes to detect abrupt drift via statistical tests on incoming data streams.
EDDM and ADWIN operate hierarchically, with EDDM detecting gradual changes and ADWIN validating and confirming drift type.
Three datasets were used: Kaggle European credit card transactions, a GCC bank real-world dataset, and UCI Spambase for non-financial benchmarking.
Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, ROC AUC, and drift detection rate metrics.
K-fold cross-validation with K=5 was used to assess model robustness across different data splits.
findings: num: 99.99% accuracy achieved on the Real Dataset with 90 features, 99.99% precision, and 99.99% drift detection rate.
num: 100% accuracy, precision, and recall on the Credit Card Dataset with 30 features during preprocessing evaluation.
num: 99.88% accuracy, 99.76% precision, and 100% recall on the Credit Card Dataset at detection stage with 30 features.
num: 93.06% accuracy and 93.54% F1 score on the Spam Dataset with 55 features, demonstrating cross-domain applicability.
num: EDDM detected 284,313 of 284,314 total drifts on the Credit Card Dataset, capturing 100% of drifts.
num: 476 abrupt drifts and 283,838 gradual drifts identified on the Credit Card Dataset.
num: 66,402 total drifts detected on the Real Dataset with 109 abrupt and 66,293 gradual drifts.
num: 2,792 drifts detected on the Spam Dataset, all captured by EDDM with 75 abrupt and 2,717 gradual drifts.
num: 5-fold cross-validation accuracy of 0.99999 on Credit Card Dataset, surpassing Kajal et al. baseline of 0.97.
key_figures_tables: Figure 12: Proposed methodology integrating CNN, EDDM, and ADWIN for fraud detection → Two-phase framework separates preprocessing from drift-aware detection.
Figure 13: Drift detection workflow using CNN, EDDM, and ADWIN with warning and out-of-control thresholds → Hierarchical approach classifies drift as gradual or abrupt.
Figure 14: Venn diagram of drift detection overlap on Credit Card Dataset → EDDM detected 100% of drifts with ADWIN confirming one gradual drift.
Table 5: Preprocessing-stage results across all datasets with varying feature counts → 90 features optimal for Real, 30 for Credit Card, 55 for Spam.
Table 6: Detection-stage results showing near-perfect metrics across all three datasets → Framework generalizes beyond financial fraud detection.
Table 11: K-fold cross-validation comparison with existing works → Proposed model outperforms prior methods in accuracy and recall.

definitions.definition: Early Drift Detection Method, monitors average distance between errors to detect gradual distribution changes in data streams.
ADaptive WINdowing, dynamically adjusts sliding window sizes via statistical tests to detect abrupt drift in streaming data.
Adaptive Synthetic Sampling, generates synthetic minority-class instances focusing on hard-to-learn regions to address class imbalance.
Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture that learns complex spatial patterns from transaction feature data.
The phenomenon where the statistical properties of data change over time, degrading model performance in streaming environments.
Mutual Information, a supervised feature selection metric measuring statistical dependence between features and target variable.
Know Your Customer, regulatory and institutional procedures for verifying customer identity in financial systems.
Anti Money Laundering, systems and processes designed to detect and prevent illegal financial transactions.
Europay Mastercard and Visa, a global standard for secure payment processing using smart card chip technology.
Fraud Detection System, automated systems designed to identify and flag fraudulent transactions in payment systems.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes an integrated preprocessing and drift detection framework that combines Mutual Information feature selection, ADASYN class balancing, and a hierarchical EDDM-ADWIN drift detection mechanism with CNN classification.
directly_justifies: EDDM and ADWIN operate hierarchically to detect both gradual and abrupt concept drift in transaction streams.
ADASYN focuses synthetic instance generation on hard-to-learn minority-class regions in imbalanced fraud datasets.
Mutual Information with SelectKBest reduces computational overhead by eliminating irrelevant and redundant transaction features.
CNN automatically identifies complex interrelations in transaction data that traditional techniques miss.
The framework achieved 99.99% accuracy and 99.99% drift detection rate on the Real Dataset with mixed data types.
EDDM detected 100% of drifts across all three evaluated datasets, confirming robust drift sensitivity.
limits: The framework does not support direct online learning for incremental adaptation without full model retraining [unacknowledged].
Dual-drift detection introduces small communication and computational overhead during validation steps.
The CNN architecture may not scale efficiently to extremely high-frequency transaction environments without lightweight alternatives.
Privacy-preserving mechanisms such as federated learning for cross-institutional fraud detection were not explored [unacknowledged].
Evaluation relied on historical datasets rather than live streaming transaction data in production environments [unacknowledged].

remember_this: Framework combines MI feature selection, ADASYN resampling, and CNN-EDDM-ADWIN for fraud detection across payment systems.
EDDM captures both gradual and abrupt concept drift, detecting 100% of drifts across all three evaluated datasets.
Near-perfect accuracy of 99.99% was achieved on a real-world mixed-type dataset with 90 selected features.
The approach generalizes beyond financial fraud, achieving 99.34% accuracy on a non-financial spam dataset.
Hierarchical drift detection with EDDM and ADWIN is the first combination of both methods for dual-type drift in fraud detection.
